title: Cell Fixation for Transmission Electron Microscopy Analysis
author: Debora Ferreira Barreto-Vieira
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jqucmww

steps.title: Wash monolayer with PBS
steps.instruction: Rinse the cell monolayer three times with 1× phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS).

steps.title: Trypsinize cells
steps.instruction: Add enough trypsin to completely cover the monolayer and incubate at 28 °C for 3 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Add enough trypsin to cover the monolayer.

steps.title: Neutralize trypsin with FBS
steps.instruction: Add fetal bovine serum (FBS) to cover the monolayer to stop trypsin activity, then discard the excess serum.

substeps.instruction: Add enough fetal bovine serum (FBS) to cover the monolayer in order to inhibit the trypsinization process.

steps.title: Dislodge cells from flask
steps.instruction: Detach the cells by slapping the side of the flask with the heel of your hand a few times.

substeps.instruction: Slap the side of the flask with the heel of your hand a few times to dislodge cells from the plastic substrate.

steps.title: Fix cells in glutaraldehyde
steps.instruction: Aliquot the detached cells into microcentrifuge tubes containing 500 µL of 1 % glutaraldehyde diluted in 0.2 M sodium cacodylate buffer.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot cells in microcentrifuge tubes containing 500 µL of glutaraldehyde 1 % diluted in sodium cacodylate buffer 0.2 M.
